standard_prerequisites.use: Makes each one-dimensional component affine under the hypothesis of the lemma.

standard_prerequisites.name: Image of an affine scheme under a finite surjective morphism is affine
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma coherent-lemma-image-affine-finite-morphism-affine-Noetherian (tag 01YQ)
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers affineness from the coproduct of the components to X.

core_obligations: Decompose X into its irreducible components and view them with the reduced induced scheme structure, so that each component is either a singleton or a curve (proof lines 9509-9512).
In the curve case use the criterion for affineness of a curve under the hypothesis that no component is proper of dimension one, so that each component is affine (proof lines 9513-9514).

Observe that the natural map from the coproduct of the components to X is finite and surjective with affine source, and conclude that X is affine by the descent of affineness along finite surjective morphisms (proof lines 9515-9518).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the irreducible components with the induced structure.
Use finiteness and surjectivity of the coproduct map to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a separated finite type scheme over a field of dimension at most one with no one-dimensional proper irreducible component is affine. The proof decomposes X into irreducible components, endows each with the reduced induced structure, observes that each component is either a singleton or a curve, and in the curve case uses the criterion relating proper curves to affineness of the curve (proof lines 9509-9514). The resulting map from the coproduct of the components to X is finite and surjective with affine source, and the image of an affine scheme under a finite surjective morphism is affine, which gives the conclusion (proof lines 9515-9518). H2: the reduction to the components and the descent of affineness along a finite surjection are the substance.
